core_obligations: Derive flatness from the definition of syntomic (proof line 8415).
Reduce the first implication to the statement that a relative global complete intersection is a local complete intersection (proof lines 8416-8420).
Show that a local complete intersection is of finite presentation because its defining ideal is finitely generated (proof lines 8423-8424).
Reduce the second implication to the base change to a field and choose a prime of the base change (proof lines 8425-8430).

Use the local definition of a Koszul regular ideal to produce a presentation, transport it through the flat base change, upgrade it to a regular sequence, and conclude by the field criterion (proof lines 8431-8451).
proof_roadmap: One direction by the local-to-global complete intersection lemma (proof lines 8414-8420).
Reduce the other direction to a field (proof lines 8423-8430).
Transport the presentation through flat base change (proof lines 8431-8444).
Upgrade to a regular sequence and conclude (proof lines 8445-8451).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies syntomic ring maps with the flat local complete intersections. One direction reduces the global complete intersection presentation to the local condition using the compatibility of the definitions. The other direction is the substance: a local complete intersection is finitely presented because the defining Koszul regular ideal is finitely generated, so it suffices to verify the condition after base change to a field, where the author writes the ring as a quotient of a polynomial ring, uses the definition of a locally Koszul regular ideal to find a local presentation, transports Koszul regularity of the generators through the flat base change to the residue situation, upgrades it to a regular sequence by the finite-module criterion, and then quotes the characterisation of local complete intersections over a field.
